title: Simulation of reading a field
statement: Let $M$ be a finite-state Boolean Turing machine, let $y$ be a Boolean word, and let $f$ and $bits$ be a Boolean and a bit vector of length equal to the number of selector types of $M$. Suppose $rest,w,r,w_C,w_O$ are Boolean words, $p$ is natural with $1\le p$, the suffix of $y$ from position $p-1$ is $rest$, and reading a field from $rest$ returns $(w,r)$. After $2|w|+2$ steps of the tabulating machine for $M$, started in state $fA(f,bits)$ at input position $\min(p,|y|+1)$ with auxiliary words $[],w_C,w_O$, its entire configuration is the configuration at input position $\min(p+2|w|+2,|y|+1)$ with state $cpy(bits)$ if $f$ is true and $fA(true,bits)$ otherwise, auxiliary words $w_C,w_O$ changed to $w_C,w_O\mathbin{+ egin{bmatrix}w\end{bmatrix}}$ if $f$ is true, and to $w_C\mathbin{+ egin{bmatrix}w\end{bmatrix}},w_O$ otherwise; the output remains empty and the original machine's work tapes remain blank.
hypotheses_covered: $M$ is a finite-state Boolean Turing machine
$bits$ has length equal to the number of selector types of $M$
the suffix of $y$ from position $p-1$ is $rest$
